newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open slightly higher.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open slightly higher Friday in line with LME copper prices despite a further small rise in LME warehouse stocks.
COMEX September copper was called unchanged to up 0.50 cent from Thursday's close of 110.90 cents a lb after trading from 111.00 to 112.10 cents on ACCESS.
COMEX copper prices have fallen more than 10 cents in the past week, retreating from 12-month highs, before finding some support.
LME copper stocks rose 150 tonnes Friday to 124,900 tonnes, while COMEX stocks fell 1,080 short tons Thursday to 48,565 short tons.
Overnight, Canada's Inco Ltd said negotiators for the 4,670 unionized workers at the company's Sudbury, Ontario, nickel and copper mine endorsed a deal to end a four week strike.
Inco produces some 90,000 tonnes a year of copper and supplies metal to the Northeastern region of the U.S.

Copper prices are seen drifting heading into the seasonally slow summer period, but Australia's Broken Hill Pty Ltd (BHP), the world's second largest copper producer, said Friday it expected recent strength in copper prices to continue into 1998.
